newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Kidnapped U.S. geologist found dead in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Kidnapped U.S. geologist found dead in Colombia.

text.p: The body of kidnapped American geologist Frank Pescatori has been found shot through the head in northern Colombia, police said on Wednesday.
Pescatori, 40, originally from New Jersey, was snatched by five unidentified gunmen on Dec. 10 at a coal mining site near the town of Hato Nuevo in northern Guajira province.

A police spokesman said Pescatori's partially decomposed body was found on Tuesday evening near the town of San Juan del Cesar, in Guajira. He appeared to have been killed with a shotgun five or six days ago, the spokesman said.
Pescatori was the head of Alabama-based mining company Geomet.

At the time it was not clear whether the geologist was kidnapped by criminals or leftist guerrillas but police now say they suspect his abductors were rebels of the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest guerrilla force.

Another American, Houston oilman Gerald Schaffer, is still missing after being kidnapped in neighbouring Venezuela by suspected Colombian guerrillas two weeks ago. Police believe his kidnappers brought him across the border into Colombia.
A Venezuelan who was snatched along with Schaffer but later released said on Wednesday that the kidnappers had mistaken the American for a wealthy oil executive.

"Because he is a North American the captors thought he was a wealthy person, when in fact he is a technician who accepted an invitation to go fishing," Eduardo Barando told the Venevision television network in Venezuela.
He said Schaffer was well but his whereabouts were unknown.
"I couldn't say in what part of Colombia we were. We were totally blindfolded and unable to communicate," he said.

Colombia has the highest rate of abductions in the world, with more than 1,300 last year. Roughly half of those have been blamed on leftist rebels seeking to fill their war chests with ransom payments to finance their fight against the state.
